focal_evidence: Corolla exsertion and lower-lip width positively predict stigmatic pollen load and seed predation; in the linked seven-population Model 2, seed predation also increases with pollen load after exsertion, lip width and population are retained.
next_test: Manipulate exsertion across levels and estimate pollination and predator components under selective P/G states.

focal_evidence: Both response routes are positive on exsertion, but published model terms use different response scales/link functions and do not provide a prospectively defined common-scale sensitivity comparison.
next_test: Estimate both functional response curves over the same randomized exsertion levels and compare predeclared common-scale derivatives/effect contrasts.

focal_evidence: P. rex is pollen limited in the focal programme and greater exsertion predicts greater pollen receipt; however standing variation does not show that antagonist-mediated selection caused reduced exsertion or the observed pollen limitation.
next_test: Test whether removing seed-predator pressure shifts the reproductive optimum toward greater exsertion and increases pollen receipt/initial seed set.

focal_evidence: Seed predation reduces final viable seed production and opposes pollinator-mediated selection, but the observational study does not identify a bounded combined optimum or show that the natural exsertion distribution sits at that optimum.
next_test: Fit the randomized z x P x G reproductive surface; test whether the natural-G combined optimum is below the predator-removed pollinator-favored optimum and whether natural phenotypes concentrate near the combined optimum.

focal_evidence: Best seed-predation model: seed predation = constant + exsertion*** + lip width* + pollen* + population*** (AICc -156.11; seven linked populations). Authors report unexpectedly greater seed predation on flowers with more stigmatic pollen.
next_test: Use matched plant blocks to test prospectively whether stronger pollination trajectories predict earlier/higher antagonist pressure after controlling randomized z and measured local state.

focal_evidence: Oviposition occurs during flowering, before final seed resources exist. The authors propose pollen odours or unmeasured floral traits as possible predictive cues and explicitly state the mechanism is unclear.
next_test: If coupling replicates prospectively, assay candidate floral odour/phenology/reward cues separately from pollen receipt and exsertion.
